Marcus —

Thanks for taking a look. We saw a ~14 minute window on Nov 3 where p95 latency for our write API in us-west spiked ~3x and a subset (~18%) of requests returned 5xx for brief bursts. Our monitoring (internal) and customer reports line up to that timestamp range: 2026-11-03T22:04:00Z — 2026-11-03T22:18:30Z.

We checked Redwood's uptime page and it looks like the minutes were excluded under a third-party CDN maintenance tag (EdgeCorp), plus probe sampling didn't flag the anomaly due to low probe fanout in us-west at that minute. We believe the majority of user traffic was impacted (our traffic logs attached) and that the event should be counted against SLO rather than excluded.

Request: please escalate to billing/SLA team for exception review (we would like a credit equivalent to the fractional availability loss). Attached: uptime-report-Nov-03.csv (our traffic breakdown) and trace-samples-utc.log (sample traces).

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the data, and for flagging the precise window. I pulled our incident timeline and the EdgeCorp maintenance notice; the maintenance window overlaps your timestamps by about 8 minutes, but our internal probes show the visible effect extending slightly beyond that.

Two notes to be explicit about how we account for this type of event:
- Exception policy: we exclude downtime that meets our "third-party maintenance" criteria when the third party publishes a scheduled maintenance window and the affected routers are tagged in their maintenance announcement.
- Apportionment: when only a subset of customer traffic is affected we use probe-weighted apportionment to estimate how much of a customer’s traffic was impacted. That means small-path microbursts can register less impact if our probe fanout missed them.

Given the overlap and the tomography differences, I'm going to escalate this for a manual review. Can you share a few more full trace IDs (grep-able) and your CDN edge container ids for the time window? That will speed reconciliation.

I'll loop in billing and Marissa for the reconciliation calculation.

— Marcus
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04 11:17 PST
Subject: Fwd: elevated p95 / partial degradations in us-west — credit request

Forwarding OrbitHealth packet. I computed a quick reconciliation using our probe logs and their shared traces. Summary:
- Event window (our probes): 2026-11-03T22:05:30Z — 2026-11-03T22:20:00Z (14.5 minutes).
- EdgeCorp maintenance window declared: 2026-11-03T22:09:00Z — 2026-11-03T22:12:00Z (3 minutes).
- Probe-weighted impacted fraction for OrbitHealth traffic: 22%.
- If we strictly apply the "third-party maintenance" exclusion we would remove the 3-minute block, leaving ~11.5 minutes counted. Apportioning the remaining minutes by the 22% impact yields ~2.53 minutes of accounted downtime for OrbitHealth.

OrbitHealth’s ask is to not apply the third-party maintenance exclusion because their customer traffic shows a larger hit and their traces indicate tail latency spikes outside the announced window. I prepared a reconciliation spreadsheet (link below) and a proposed partial credit: 0.6% of monthly invoice (equivalent to 2.5 minutes weighted) or, alternatively, a one-time service credit of the same dollar amount.

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/oh-debug-report
Attachment: proposed-recon-Nov03.csv (inlined in our ticket)

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: elevated p95 / partial degradations in us-west — credit request

Quick thoughts from SLO/accounting side:
- The policy language for third-party maintenance is intentionally strict because otherwise we'd end up double-counting. It requires: published schedule, named affected routers, and matching path fingerprints in our telemetry. EdgeCorp's announcement ticks two boxes but their fingerprint list omitted one of the US-WEST nodes that shows up in OrbitHealth traces.
- For severity thresholds, our SLO is p99 availability but we use p95 latency for operational alerts. OrbitHealth's observed p95 spike doesn't by itself trigger a full-availability bucket unless we have user-facing errors/crash rate. They did report ~18% 5xx; that matters.

Proposal: do a manual apportionment override where we treat the full 14.5 minute window as eligible but only grant credit proportional to traffic impact as corroborated by both parties' traces. That yields a 2.8-minute weighted impact in our numbers compared to Marissa's 2.53. I recommend offering a 0.7% invoice credit and closing with a postmortem documenting the missing EdgeCorp router in their announcement.

If accepted, Ben should handle the billing credit and we need to notify EdgeCorp to amend their maintenance post.

Neha
Head of Product Reliability, Redwood Inference

- Credit: 0.7% applied to your Nov invoice OR a one-off service credit of the same value (your choice).
